patients.label: 60-year-old man with L2-3 upper lumbar disc herniation treated with PELD under intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring

identity_evidence.quote: A 60-year-old male patient was admitted to our department

attribution_limitations: The one-month JOA and ODI values are stated in the sentence after the "One month after the surgery" VAS sentence; their own sentence names no time.

The baseline VAS, JOA and ODI sentences and the physical examination sentences state no time; they follow the admission sentence in the case paragraph. Only the later phrase "the VAS decreased from 8 to 0" places a VAS of 8 before awakening.
One grade (4/5) is given for the left quadriceps and the first toe; the side of the first toe is not stated separately.
The discussion states that intraoperative MEP improvement was found in one of nine PELD cases with IONM; the other eight cases are not described.
The text says MRI and CT jointly revealed the compression, while the captions assign the MRI and CT findings to separate figures; no time or date for these studies is given.
The Highlights and Conclusion say MEP increase "can be considered" an improvement of the treated levels; this is an author interpretation from one case.
Anterior thigh pain is stated only in a discussion sentence about this case, alongside pain for more than 10 years; the sentence does not give the thigh pain its own duration or side.
